properties.name: link_artifact stops rewriting an artifact's name on every re-link — the half of BL-166 that was left because the field could not be omitted
properties.rationale:
PRECEDENT, FOUND BY SEARCHING RATHER THAN REASONED FROM SCRATCH. This is at least the fourth occurrence of one class, and the class has been fixed three times before: BL-46 (a partial edit resetting a verified capability to planned), BL-166 (link_artifact re-materializing defaults through create_node, dropping last_confirmed_at), BL-183 (every add_* constructor writing a subset and resetting the rest), and set_verification_status deleting last_run_at on omission, fixed 2026-08-09. Three sibling setters state the convention outright: omitting one leaves it alone.

WHY IT RECURRED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. The class already has a guard — constructors_preserve.rs. Every case in it was an `add_*` constructor, and its own header asserted that link_artifact "was fixed for this in BL-166". Membership was drawn on HOW THE CALL IS SPELLED rather than on WHAT IT DOES: build a node from a partial property set. So a write path with identical behaviour under a different name sat outside the guard while the guard's header vouched for it. A hand-drawn boundary around a behavioural class is what let a fixed defect stay half-fixed for three weeks.

AND THE GUARD FILE WAS NOT REGISTERED AS AN ARTIFACT until this change, so nothing in the design connected it to the four defects it exists to catch, and its scope error was invisible to every report that reads the artifact layer.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, stated so nobody inherits a wrong answer that looks settled. How many stored artifact names were already flattened by past re-links is unmeasured: build_design_graph.py re-links 34 artifacts on every run and would have rewritten each to whatever string that script holds, but no before-and-after record survives to compare against. And the guard's membership is still hand-maintained — nothing yet detects a NEW write path that builds a node from a partial property set, so the next member will be found the way this one was, by somebody tripping over it.
properties.summary:
THE OBSERVATION, before any explanation. Linking an existing Artifact to a second target on 2026-09-07 was refused with `missing field name`, and the call then required the artifact's full name and location to be re-sent — text the graph already held and had returned moments earlier. NOT AFFECTED: artifact_type, location, checksum, content_ref and note_kind, all of which preserve a stored value when omitted.

THE CAUSE, READ FROM THE CODE. write_artifact_link upserts the Artifact with `.set("name", …)` — unconditional — while every field beside it uses set_opt. Because the surface made `name` mandatory, "leave the name alone" was inexpressible: every re-link rewrote the name to whatever the caller happened to re-type, and the refusal that demanded it invited a stub. The comment directly above that write argues at length that re-registering must never erase what the design already knows. The reasoning was applied to the fields a caller could omit and stopped at the one they could not.

THE FIX, AT THE CAUSE. The name in effect is RESOLVED — the caller's if given, otherwise the one the design already holds. The Artifact's name is written only when the caller passed one, so omitting it preserves the stored value. A FIRST link, where there is nothing to resolve, is refused and the refusal names what would have worked. `description` is accepted here too, so registering a file and describing it is one call rather than two tools with different field sets for the same node.

⚠️ THE FIRST VERSION OF THE FIX WAS ITSELF INCOMPLETE, and it is worth recording because it is the same shape one level down. Making `name` merely optional left the provenance Fragment's `title` — a REQUIRED property — with nothing to build from, so a re-link onto an Artifact whose Fragment did not yet exist failed schema validation on a field the caller had never mentioned. That is why the name is resolved rather than just optional. It was caught by using the fix on this change's own bookkeeping, not by a gate, and it now has its own case: `re_linking_mints_a_missing_fragment_from_the_stored_name`.

OBSERVED TO FAIL FIRST, by negative control: restoring the unconditional write failed `re_linking_an_artifact_does_not_rename_it` on exactly the data-loss assertion, while the other cases — including both controls pinning that an explicitly-passed name STILL renames — stayed green.

DEMONSTRATED ON REAL DATA. The guard file's own Artifact was then linked to `req:intent-preserved` with no name and no location passed, and its 108-character name, its description and its location all survived.
